In an ideal gas intermolecular forces are assumed to be zero, so the potential energy of an ideal gas is zero (while the potential energy of a real gas is not zero).

The temperature of the gas is unchanged, so the average velocity of the gas particles is unchanged. 

As a result of a decrease in volume, the gas atoms collide with the walls more frequently.

This means that the rate of change of momentum at the container wall increases, hence pressure increases.

question.html:
A container is filled with an ideal, monatomic gas and sealed with a movable piston. The volume of the gas is m, the temperature of the gas is C and the pressure of the gas is Pa.

a. Outline the difference between the internal energy of an ideal gas and the internal energy of a real gas. 

  [2]

b. Find the number of gas atoms in the container.

  [2]

The piston on the container is moved so that the volume of the container decreases by %. The temperature of the gas is kept unchanged.

c. Calculate the new pressure of the gas.

  [1]

d. Explain, in terms of molecular motion, this change in pressure. 

  [2]
